Definition: a flag; also a sail; by implication, a flagstaff; generally a signal; figuratively, a token
BiblicalUsage: Moses is told to set a fiery serpent on a pole so that everyone bitten may look and live, and Isaiah sees a root of Jesse standing as an ensign for the peoples. The LORD promises to lift His hand to the Gentiles and set up His standard, and Jeremiah calls for a standard to be raised in the land.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the standard is lifted so that the bitten may look and live. The pole in the wilderness, the root of Jesse, and the banner over the nations all say the same thing — look to what God has lifted up.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
